codeReview.summary: The fetch error handling, worktree-targeted .gitignore update, and absolute home_dir fallback are implemented as requested. However, the attached-registry persistence change does not make read-modify-write operations safe under concurrent writers.

issues.description: register_attached/unregister_attached still perform unlocked read-modify-write against .attached_registry.json, and save_attached_registry writes to a shared fixed temp path (.attached_registry.json.tmp). Under concurrent writes this can lose updates and can fail on tmp-path rename races, so the concurrency-safety requirement for registry persistence is not fully satisfied.
test_registry_concurrent_access is sequential and does not execute concurrent register/unregister operations, so it cannot validate the claimed concurrent-write safety behavior.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The rust-worker skill requires RED-first TDD (write failing tests before implementation), but the worker transcript shows implementation edits were done before tests were added, while handoff.skillFeedback still reports followedProcedure=true.

summary: Review failed. Three fixes are correct, but attached-registry persistence is still race-prone under concurrent read-modify-write operations, and the added concurrency test does not exercise real concurrency.
